solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: North Italian drinking with assistant (6,3)

indicators.note: the Italian takes in the next letter as if swallowing it

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
Umberto is an Italian first name
w = with, as in w/

annotation.surface: A man from northern Italy out having a drink with his assistant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Italian' is any Italian man, here Umberto, and he 'drinks' the W for 'with' just before his last letter. A number two is a deputy or second-in-command.
annotation.definitionFit: A number two is the person ranked just below the boss, an assistant or deputy.

clue.text: Ornament in mostly pleasant facility (4-4)

indicators.note: most of the word, so its last letter goes

blocks.note: NICE without its last letter
a facility for something is a knack for it

annotation.surface: Someone admiring an ornament in a nice building or venue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Facility' reads as a building, but it means a skill, a knack. Nick-nack is a less common spelling of knick-knack.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: knick-knacks, here in the older nick-nack spelling, are trinkets kept for show.

clue.text: Chap’s neck hair cut (3)

indicators.note: a cut shortens the word, taking off its last letter

blocks.note: MANE, the hair on a horse's neck, with its last letter cut

annotation.surface: A man's neck hair has been trimmed at the barber's.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a haircut, and 'cut' really does trim the word: the mane loses its end.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: chap is informal British for a man, as in 'a decent chap'.

clue.text: Metal pick’s head covered by earth (8)

indicators.note: the first letter is covered over by another, so E takes the place of P

blocks.note: a plectrum is a guitar pick
E = earth, as on an electric plug
the head of PLECTRUM, P, is covered over by E

annotation.surface: A miner's pickaxe with its head buried in the soil as it digs for metal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pick' looks like a miner's tool, but it is the plectrum a guitarist plucks with. Replace its first letter P with E.
annotation.definitionFit: Electrum is a natural alloy of gold and silver, a metal.

clue.text: Give an account of folk hero (4)

blocks.note: to narrate or relate a story
the Swiss archer who shot an apple off his son's head

annotation.surface: Asking someone to recount the story of a folk hero.
annotation.walkthrough: William Tell is the Swiss archer of legend.
annotation.definitionFit: To tell something is to give an account of it; Tell is also the legendary Swiss hero.

clue.text: What free traders want: better country, but without leaders (4,6)

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its leading letter

blocks.note: TOP, to better someone, without its leader T
DENMARK without its leader D
YET, meaning but, without its leader Y

annotation.surface: A free-trade manifesto: a better country would come from doing without its leaders.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Better' is the verb to top, not a comparative, and 'but' must be read as yet. All three lose their first letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Free traders want an open market, one without tariffs or barriers.

clue.text: Penny and Henry, perhaps, claiming daughter is expert (6)

indicators.note: to claim something is to take it for yourself, so UNIT takes in D

blocks.note: p = penny
the henry is the unit of inductance
standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: Two people, Penny and Henry, insisting their daughter is an expert.
annotation.walkthrough: Penny and Henry look like a couple. The henry is a physics unit, hence 'perhaps' marking it as one example of a unit.
annotation.definitionFit: A pundit is an expert, especially one who gives opinions in the media.

clue.text: Son can get stopped, primarily, in police operations (6)

indicators.note: take the first letter of each of the two words before it

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
a tin is a can
the first letters of Get and Stopped

annotation.surface: A son could be caught and stopped in a police raid.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can' is a noun here, a tin, not the verb it seems.
annotation.definitionFit: Stings are undercover police operations that trap criminals.

clue.text: First-class setter beginning to take plunge (7)

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word, its first letter

blocks.note: a plum job is a first-class one
the setter refers to themself as me
the first letter of Take

annotation.surface: A top-class diver starting to take the plunge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Setter' is the crossword setter, who is ME in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs describe falling fast and far, like a diver or a share price.

clue.text: Second African national smuggling Charlie for another (10)

definitions.note: The answer is another African national, so 'another' stands for the whole idea.

indicators.note: smugglers hide goods inside, so ZAMBIAN hides the C

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a person from Zambia
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A second African citizen caught smuggling cocaine on behalf of someone else.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' is slang for cocaine in the surface, but just C here. The definition is the bare word 'another': another African national, a neighbour of Zambia.
annotation.definitionFit: A Mozambican is from Mozambique, which borders Zambia, so another African national.

clue.text: Hide scam with proof of authenticity for auditor (7)

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the words are to be heard

blocks.note: a con is a scam; a seal proves a document is genuine

annotation.surface: Covering up a scam with a forged certificate so the accountant checking the books won't notice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' reads as an accountant checking the books; here it is simply a listener.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean keeping something out of sight.

clue.text: Eighty winks? An indefinite number? Thirteen? (4,5)

blocks.note: forty winks is a nap, so eighty winks is a long doze
n stands for any number in maths

annotation.surface: A string of three puzzled questions, like someone muttering over a sum.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark on 'Eighty winks?' flags the joke of doubling forty winks. A long dozen, like a baker's dozen, is thirteen.
annotation.definitionFit: A long dozen is thirteen, one more than a dozen; the question mark admits it is a less familiar term.

clue.text: Deny Nick in London has lost weight (6)

indicators.note: the word loses the letter that follows

blocks.note: Newgate was a London prison, and nick is slang for prison
standard abbreviation, removed

annotation.surface: Someone denying that a man called Nick in London has slimmed down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a man's name; it is British slang for a prison. Newgate was London's notorious old jail.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the logical sense: ruling a statement false is denying it.

clue.text: Attempt to convert try, and stretch one’s back to prepare (10)

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: to have a go is to try
a spell is a stretch of time
I = one, plus the S
the last letter of preparE

annotation.surface: Rugby talk: a player tries to convert a try, stretching his back to get ready for the kick.
annotation.walkthrough: The rugby surface makes 'convert' and 'try' look like scoring terms. Here convert is religious and try is just a go.
annotation.definitionFit: To gospellise is to preach the gospel to people, attempting to convert them.

clue.text: Romeo is in with doctor about mother’s problem with hydration (6,4)

indicators.note: the doctor goes around the mother

blocks.note: Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet
used literally
used literally
a GP is a family doctor
a dam is an animal's mother

annotation.surface: Romeo consulting a doctor about his mother being dehydrated.
annotation.walkthrough: The medical surface makes hydration a bodily matter; the problem is in a building's walls. Rising damp is water soaking up from the ground into brickwork, a familiar complaint in old British houses.
annotation.definitionFit: Rising damp is a building's problem with water creeping up its walls, too much hydration.

clue.text: Phoebe’s granddaughter uncovered difficult Times cryptic (7)

indicators.note: with its cover, the outer letters, taken off
the letters of TIMES are made obscure, jumbled

blocks.note: HARD without its outer letters
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A self-referential boast: even a goddess's granddaughter would find today's Times cryptic hard.
annotation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the Titan Phoebe was mother of Leto, whose twins were Apollo and Artemis. 'Cryptic' is doing the jumbling, not describing the puzzle.
annotation.definitionFit: Artemis was the daughter of Leto, whose mother was the Titan Phoebe.

clue.text: Designer’s outlay? I’m not sure that is right (9)

blocks.note: an outlay is a cost
the hesitant noise 'um'
i.e. = that is
standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: Someone querying a designer's expenses and doubting the figure is right.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I'm not sure' is spoken hesitation, UM, and 'that is' is the Latin abbreviation i.e.
annotation.definitionFit: The designer here works in theatre or film wardrobe, making and supplying what the actors wear.

clue.text: Perhaps sparkly kilts are unusual (8)

indicators.note: the letters are put into an unusual order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A remark that glittery kilts are a rare sight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' warns that sparkly is only one way of being starlike.
annotation.definitionFit: Something starlike shines like a star, which is one way of being sparkly.

clue.text: Weapon of Scottish fighter Ali, once again (8)

blocks.note: Muhammad Ali was once Cassius Clay
more = again, as in once more

annotation.surface: A Scottish fighter's weapon, compared with the boxer Ali once more.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fighter' pulls towards Ali the boxer, but it belongs to the definition. Ali fought as Cassius Clay before changing his name.
annotation.definitionFit: A claymore is the great two-handed sword of Scottish Highland warriors.

clue.text: Dialect in Barking is exactly the same (9)

indicators.note: barking mad, so the letters go crazy

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A claim that the accent in Barking, an east London district, is just like another.
annotation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of east London, so the surface reads as a place. As an indicator it means barking mad.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: two things matching in every detail are exactly the same.

clue.text: Maybe Trump snubbed new tanning agent (7)

indicators.note: snub-nosed, with the end cut short

blocks.note: MELANIA, one Trump, without her last letter
standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A Trump cold-shouldering a new fake-tan product.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Maybe Trump' means one member of the family, Melania, not Donald.
annotation.definitionFit: Melanin is the skin pigment that darkens as you tan.

clue.text: Insufficient silver in lake (6)

indicators.note: the silver sits inside the lake

blocks.note: a mere is a lake
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

annotation.surface: Not enough silver found at the bottom of the lake.
annotation.walkthrough: MERE is an old word for a lake, common in English place names like Windermere.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a scanty portion is too small for the need.

clue.text: Onus, essentially, on work that’s obtained by exerting significant pressure (3,3)

definitions.text: that’s obtained by exerting significant pressure
definitions.note: The definition describes the answer as 'that which is obtained', a noun clause standing for the noun.

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its centre

blocks.note: the middle letters of oNUs
toil is hard work

annotation.surface: The burden of hard work that you only get through by putting yourself under real pressure.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means the first piece sits above the second. The pressure is the press that squeezes oil from nuts.
annotation.definitionFit: Nut oil is extracted by pressing nuts hard.

clue.text: Label unknown spirit (6)

blocks.note: a brand is a label
x, y and z are unknowns in algebra

annotation.surface: A bottle of spirit with an unfamiliar label.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unknown' is one of the algebra letters, here Y.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the one distilled from wine, among the spirits alongside gin and whisky.

clue.text: Athenian statesman in capital, powerless to lead trends (9)

indicators.note: P for power is taken away
the capital's letters go at the front, ahead of the trends

blocks.note: PARIS without P, power
the tide of opinion is its trend

annotation.surface: A Greek statesman in a capital city, with no power to set the fashion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To lead' tells you ARIS comes first. Aristides 'the Just' was an Athenian statesman and general of the fifth century BC.
annotation.definitionFit: Aristides was a leading statesman of ancient Athens.

clue.text: Mark has carried boxes (4)

indicators.note: the phrase encloses the answer as a box holds its contents

blocks.note: haS CARried

annotation.surface: A man named Mark has been lugging boxes about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' looks like the thing carried; it is a verb, meaning encloses.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the mark a healed wound leaves on the skin.

clue.text: City’s fashionable past (7)

blocks.note: chic = stylish, fashionable
long ago = in the past

annotation.surface: A city whose stylish days are behind it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'City's' reads as possessive; the 's is 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Windy City of Illinois.

clue.text: Naked servant is bitter? (3)

indicators.note: stripped of its outer covering, the first and last letters

blocks.note: VALET with its outer letters V and T removed

annotation.surface: A servant caught unclothed feels resentful.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' looks like the servant's mood; it is the British beer. The question mark flags that bitter is just one kind of ale.
annotation.definitionFit: Bitter is a type of ale, a British pale beer.

clue.text: Watery discharge contains nickel and another metal (7)

indicators.note: the discharge holds the nickel inside it

blocks.note: rheum is a watery discharge from the eyes or nose
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

annotation.surface: A sample of runny discharge found to contain traces of nickel and another metal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Another' refers back to nickel: the answer is a second metal.
annotation.definitionFit: Rhenium is a rare metallic element.

clue.text: Soldier on a grave (9)

blocks.note: a = per, as in once a day
grave = serious, severe

annotation.surface: A soldier lying on a grave.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Soldier' a noun and 'grave' a burial place; soldier on is a verb, and grave means serious.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to soldier on is to keep going through hardship, as troops march on.
